evidence: The user's answers in the local-symmetry interview, 2026-10-24. (4a) An answer that claims a group-subgroup relation that doesn't hold gets a warning under it; (3) a lowering is described by the operations lost, the group-subgroup index and its type, t (translationengleiche) or k (klassengleiche). No check read a relation, and no tool states the index or the type. Taken as: where the run knows both groups (the context's ladder, each rung's point group, operations in the cell and rank tight to loose; detect_symmetry's facts), the ladder's rungs are nested (symmetry.js groupsByThreshold only adds operations as the tolerance grows), so H is a subgroup of G when it is tighter, with fewer operations of the cell, which G's count divides; the index is |G|/|H| in the same cell; t when the translations per cell (operations over the point group's order) stay, k when the point group stays, else neither, and a subgroup that is neither is never maximal (Hermann's theorem: every maximal subgroup is t or k). On the Demo: P-42_1m (8 operations) in F-43m (96), index 12, translations 4 to 1 per cell and point group -43m to -42m (3 x 4): neither t nor k. Where the run knows one group or none (a published phase), only the point groups are read: the 32 point groups' subgroup diagram (ITA Vol. A; each maximal subgroup listed, closed transitively; every subgroup's order divides its parent's, checked for all 32 x 32 pairs), and the point group of a symbol however written (pointGroupOfSymbol: all 230 groups of the app's table read correctly with their screws marked, and unmarked rightly or not at all: P4322 and P32 are ambiguous without the marks and give none). A subgroup's point group must be one of the parent's subgroups ('F-43m to P4/mmm' cannot be: 4/mmm has the inversion -43m lacks), a k-subgroup keeps it, a t-subgroup lowers it by its index ('I-42m, t3 of F-43m' holds). (4b) An answer that claims a cell doubling the box's average structure can't support gets a warning under it; with step 4: against a published cell-doubled phase the box can't hold, compare only what it can represent and say it can neither confirm nor rule out the phase. Taken as: a doubling along axes the box (the run's supercell) is odd along, or along every axis when the claim names none, in a sentence about the run, unless the answer says the box cannot hold it; and a doubling along axes no ordered zone-boundary point of analyze_modulations doubles (with no ordered point at all, the superstructure check's). The Demo's box is 10 x 10 x 10 and every dev case's even, so no record is affected. (6) The CIF export is labelled 'average-structure model of an RMC configuration', never a refined structure: the header's first line and _audit_creation_method say so (before: 'Symmetry-averaged RMC average structure', never 'refined' either). Known answers: answerChecks.test.js (nine wrong relations flagged by the ladder or the point groups, ten right, negated, asked or upward ones left; four doublings an odd box cannot hold flagged, six left; a doubling along axes the ordered point does not double), pointGroups.test.js, cifWriter.test.js. On the answer corpus (ten real answers) the checks raise no finding (the gemma4 space-group answer's 'transition from F-43m to P-42_1m' is no lowering claim and holds anyway). Two scripted replays pin answers 4a and 4b on the Demo. Arms A, A+ and D on the dev set before and after: all 45 records identical in verdict, score and readings. What the model is sent is unchanged. Approved by the user, 2026-10-24.
